probes.question: Which sleep stage is believed to help memories of facts and events?
True or false: Jenkins and Dallenbach found retention was better after sleep than after the same time awake.

image.alt: A ginger and white cat sleeps stretched out on a striped mattress in the sun beside a building.

body.claim: Memories hold up better after sleep than after the same time spent awake.
body.why: In 1924, Jenkins and Dallenbach found that retention was much better after a period of sleep than after the same interval awake. Slow-wave sleep is believed to help declarative memories (facts and events), while REM sleep is believed to help non-declarative memories, though results are not fully consistent.
